questions.question: The accounting equation states:
options: ASSETS equal OWNER'S EQUITY plus LIABILITIES — at every moment, after every transaction

questions.question: Every transaction has two equal effects because:
options: The equation must stay level — double entry is the arithmetic of the equation defending itself
One entry is always an estimate

questions.question: On the debit-credit compass, assets, expenses and drawings:
options: Increase on the debit side; equity, liabilities and income increase on the credit side
Increase on whichever side is empty

questions.question: The owner deposits R10 000 capital. The double entry is:
options: Debit Bank R10 000 (asset up), credit Capital R10 000 (equity up)

questions.question: A credit sale of R2 400 to Mrs Dube is recorded in:
options: The Debtors Journal, from the duplicate invoice

questions.question: Under the perpetual system, the CRJ records a cash sale of R6 900 together with:
options: Cost of sales R4 600 — the sale AND the shelf's loss together

questions.question: Goods returned BY a debtor and goods returned TO a supplier go, respectively, to:
options: Debtors Allowances Journal (credit note) and Creditors Allowances Journal (debit note)

questions.question: The two facts that choose the correct journal are:
options: The customer's name and the month
The VAT rate and the discount
Cash or credit, and which direction the value moves

subtopics.title: Posting, Balancing and the Trial Balance That Proves It

questions.question: The month's bank balance is:
options: R8 600 debit — receipts R17 900 less payments R9 300

questions.question: Trading stock ends the month at:
options: R2 000 debit — in 5 000 plus 3 000 plus the R200 returned; out 4 600 plus 1 600 as cost of sales

questions.question: The trial balance totals:
options: R20 000 on each side — bank, stock, debtors, cost of sales, rent and wages against capital, sales and creditors

questions.question: Equal trial balance totals CANNOT detect:
options: A casting error in one account
An entry posted to the WRONG account, or a transaction left out on both sides

questions.question: The debtors control account and the debtors list differ in source:
options: Control is built from JOURNAL TOTALS; the individual accounts from INDIVIDUAL POSTINGS — same street, counted twice
Control comes from the bank statement
The list comes from the trial balance
Both come from the same postings, so agreement proves nothing

questions.question: The month's debtors control balance is:
options: R1 100 — sales 2 400 less allowances 300 less receipts 1 000, agreeing with Mrs Dube's account

questions.question: A receipt posted to the wrong customer's page disturbs:
options: The LIST but not the control — the journal total that feeds the control was correct

questions.question: The creditors mirror ends the month at:
options: R1 000 credit — purchases 3 000 less payments 2 000, agreeing with the wholesaler's account

questions.question: The two questions that sort every slip are:
options: Did cash move or a promise, and which way did the value travel?
How big is the amount, and who signed it?
Is it VAT-inclusive, and is it dated?
Is it a sale, and is it profitable?

questions.question: The wholesaler's invoice of R3 000 belongs in:
options: The invoice-in box — a promise, value coming in from the supplier

questions.question: The slip that fits none of the six ordinary boxes goes to:
options: The catch-all box — the General Journal for corrections, write-offs and interest

subtopics.title: The Month That Adds Up Twice

questions.question: The ledger answers a question the shoebox cannot:
options: Where do we STAND — one page per thing, each with its balance, instead of slips by date

questions.question: The level scale at R20 000 a side proves:
options: The PAIRS were equal — every debit had its matching credit

questions.question: A slip stolen BEFORE it reaches the shoebox:
options: Steals invisibly, as far as the scale knows — both sides are short by the same nothing
Is caught by the trial balance

questions.question: The two records of the trust-buying street are:
options: The exercise book with a page per customer, and the single total line built from journal totals
The till tape and the bank statement
Two copies of the same list

questions.question: When the two counts disagree, the difference:
options: Gives directions — a wrong-page posting damages the book, a miscast journal damages the total line

questions.question: Two independent records forced to face each other monthly is valuable because:
options: It doubles the work and halves the errors automatically
Two witnesses who never compared notes telling the same story make the books BELIEVABLE
It is required only in large companies

questions.question: The year's whole machine, in order, is:
options: Only journals and a trial balance
Sort the slips; write the diaries; gather the ledger; weigh the trial balance; count the street twice
